title: Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation
authors_year: Andrew W. Lo, Harry Mamaysky, Jiang Wang (2000)
learned: Some algorithmically defined patterns contain incremental information in daily US equity returns. A pattern label is not proof of a profitable trade.
implemented: Versioned, deterministic opening-range/VWAP/EMA/ADX/volume setup with recorded conditions instead of a subjective or additive indicator vote.
not_implemented: The paper's kernel-regression pattern algorithm and empirical replication. Our breakout rule is a separate hypothesis, not a replication.
limitations: Daily US data, not NSE intraday; does not validate our indicators, thresholds or net-of-cost returns.
verification: Primary NBER abstract and bibliographic record read; full PDF not extracted.

title: Long-term correlations and multifractal analysis of trading volumes for Chinese stocks
authors_year: Guo-Hua Mu, Wei Chen, Janos Kertesz, Wei-Xing Zhou (2009 preprint; 2010 publication)
learned: One-minute volumes show systematic intraday seasonality; the observed Chinese-market pattern was not a universal U-shape.
implemented: Relative volume compares the latest completed bar with the same clock-time slot over prior observed sessions, excludes today and exposes sample count.
not_implemented: The paper's multifractal/correlation estimation; NSE-specific seasonality research.
limitations: 22 Shenzhen stocks in 2003, with different trading hours. Five baseline sessions and 1.2x threshold are engineering starting choices, not results from this paper.
verification: Primary arXiv record and readable paper sections 2 and 3.1 examined.

title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
authors_year: David H. Bailey, Jonathan M. Borwein, Marcos Lopez de Prado, Qiji Jim Zhu (2016 online publication)
learned: Selecting among many backtested strategies can overfit; an ordinary holdout alone can be unreliable.
implemented: Record actual settings and methodology version per analysis; label settings unvalidated instead of automatically optimizing them.
not_implemented: Backtesting, a registry of all optimization trials, CSCV/PBO estimation, chronological holdouts, fees/slippage evaluation.
limitations: No future-performance guarantee. Configuration logging alone does not solve overfitting.
verification: Publisher abstract and DOI 10.21314/JCF.2016.322 metadata checked; full derivation not read.

title: Real-Time Price Discovery in Stock, Bond and Foreign Exchange Markets
authors_year: Torben G. Andersen, Tim Bollerslev, Francis X. Diebold, Clara Vega (2005 working paper)
learned: High-frequency price responses to macroeconomic surprises depend on market/economic context; the same news need not have a fixed directional meaning.
implemented: Keep financial context separate from technical direction; store source/publication/receipt timestamps and gate manually entered high-impact event windows.
not_implemented: Actual-versus-consensus surprise feed, macro-regime estimation, empirical replication or a real-time event API.
limitations: International futures/US announcements, not NSE single-stock cash trading. Blackout windows are conservative policy, not an optimized result of the paper.
verification: Primary NBER abstract and bibliographic record read.

title: What Moves Stock Prices?
authors_year: David M. Cutler, James M. Poterba, Lawrence H. Summers (1988 working paper)
learned: Recorded macroeconomic news explains only part of market-return variation; large moves can occur without identifiable major news.
implemented: Missing financial/event coverage remains unknown. Manual event review is labelled incomplete coverage, not proof that no event risk exists.
not_implemented: The paper's return-decomposition exercise or a comprehensive news/sentiment model.
limitations: Historical aggregate evidence, not an intraday predictor and not evidence that fundamentals are irrelevant.
verification: Primary NBER abstract read; full PDF not extracted.

title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings?
learned: The research investigates information in the accrual and cash-flow components of earnings. Earnings composition deserves separate examination from the profit headline.
implemented: For eligible nonfinancial statements with matched periods, expose operating-cash-flow/profit and a cash-based accrual proxy: (net profit minus operating cash flow) / average assets. Record operands and eligibility.
not_implemented: Sloan's original empirical strategy/specification, a trading score, or return prediction.
limitations: The proxy is our accounting feature, not a replication. Income and cash flow must share period and scope. A positive accrual proxy alone is not fraud, low quality or a sell signal.
verification: Publisher-deposited bibliographic metadata and short abstract verified through Crossref; detailed persistence/return results were not re-read. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: The Quality of Accruals and Earnings: The Role of Accrual Estimation Errors
authors_year: Patricia M. Dechow, Ilia D. Dichev (2002)
learned: Accruals involve cash-flow estimates; estimation errors matter for earnings quality. The published measure involves past, current and future operating cash flows.
implemented: Keep accounting ratios descriptive; require aligned periods and point-in-time information. Do not label every accrual bad or insert future cash flows into live calculations.
not_implemented: The paper's regression/residual earnings-quality measure or empirical replication.
limitations: The retrospective measure is not directly a live intraday feature. Our simple cash-based proxy is not the Dechow-Dichev model.
verification: Publisher-deposited bibliography and abstract read via Crossref. Full paper specifications not reverified. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: Investor Inattention and Friday Earnings Announcements
learned: The published abstract reports weaker immediate and stronger delayed responses around Friday earnings announcements, consistent with attention affecting response timing.
implemented: Store actual announcement time and pre-announcement expectation time separately; keep immediate event risk distinct from later price response.
not_implemented: A Friday strategy, attention model, delayed-return forecast or paper replication.
limitations: Not an NSE intraday calibration. Working-paper and published estimates differ; no effect sizes were imported.
verification: Published abstract and primary NBER working-paper abstract at https://www.nber.org/papers/w11683 read. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: Value Investing: The Use of Historical Financial Statement Information to Separate Winners from Losers
learned: A longer-horizon financial-statement research reference to consider, not evidence of an intraday fair-price method.
implemented: Display separate profitability, cash-flow and balance-sheet context rather than inventing a single daily fundamental score.
not_implemented: Piotroski F-score, high-book-to-market portfolio selection, the original study or any intraday F-score strategy.
limitations: Only the bibliography was verified in this session. Do not treat this citation as verified support for our chosen ratios or thresholds.
verification: Stanford institutional bibliography and DOI 10.2307/2672906 metadata verified; institutional page had no abstract and full methodology/results were not read. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?
authors_year: Victor L. Bernard, Jacob K. Thomas (1989)
learned: A follow-up reference about post-announcement response; its title and bibliography do not establish a same-session trading rule.
implemented: Preserve comparable reported EPS and sourced pre-release expectations, with explicit surprise arithmetic and announcement timestamps. These are engineering features, not the paper's verified equations.
not_implemented: PEAD trading, standardized earnings surprise, delayed-return estimates or original empirical replication.
limitations: No guarantee that an earnings surprise causes continuation today. Basic/diluted, currency, reporting/split basis and periods must be comparable.
verification: Bibliography verified through Crossref; full text inaccessible and empirical specifications not verified. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading
learned: In a theoretical market with an informed trader, noise traders and market makers, noise trading conceals informed activity.
implemented: Keep price/volume participation separate from sourced institutional disclosures. Do not recover investor identities or intentions from unsigned candles.
not_implemented: Kyle lambda, signed-order-flow estimation, causal price-impact calibration or insider identification.
limitations: A theoretical model, not proof that institutions control all price movement or an NSE identification algorithm.
verification: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record read. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: The Behavior of Stock Prices Around Institutional Trades
authors_year: Louis K. C. Chan, Josef Lakonishok (1995)
learned: The abstract describes identified trades from investment managers grouped into packages; impact/cost relates to capitalization, relative package size and execution demands.
implemented: Retain named disclosed deal rows, quantity, price, notional and source separately. Expose scope/identity limits rather than assigning a causal impact or institutional-strength score.
not_implemented: Trade-package reconstruction, execution-cost estimation, causal impact or replication using identified manager records.
limitations: The researchers had identified institutional trade data. Our manual public disclosures and OHLCV are not equivalent data.
verification: Publisher-deposited abstract and bibliography read via Crossref. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: The Impact of Institutional Trading on Stock Prices
authors_year: Josef Lakonishok, Andrei Shleifer, Robert W. Vishny (1992)
learned: The NBER precursor studies quarterly pension-fund holdings and reports little substantial herding/positive-feedback trading except in small stocks; conclusions are sample-specific.
implemented: Keep quarterly ownership dates and percentage-point changes separate from market-wide flows and daily deals. Do not call common ownership changes proof of coordination.
not_implemented: Investor-level herding measures, quarterly trade reconstruction or any assertion of market control.
limitations: Historical quarterly pension-fund evidence, not all institutions or intraday NSE behaviour. Percentage changes can arise from denominator/corporate-action changes.
verification: Journal bibliography and 1991 NBER precursor abstract at https://www.nber.org/papers/w3846 verified. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: Disclosure of trade details of bulk deals
learned: Official reference for the bulk-deal disclosure mechanism.
implemented: A manual BULK record type with source, publication time, named participant and reported trade details.
not_implemented: Automatic disclosure collection or threshold/deadline certification.
limitations: The app does not determine whether a transaction legally qualifies as a bulk deal; it preserves the supplied source classification.
verification: Official title/date and PDF link verified; operative PDF provisions not readable. Current NSE bulk/block pages timed out. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: Review of Block Deal Framework
learned: A 2025 framework update exists; relying only on the 2017 framework would be unsafe.
implemented: Store the source's BLOCK classification without hard-coding unverified thresholds, price bands or reporting deadlines.
not_implemented: Regulatory eligibility validation, current window rules or automated exchange ingestion.
limitations: This reference is not a certification that a manually entered record meets current regulation.
verification: Official title, date, circular number and PDF link verified; operative provisions and effective dates not read. Checked 2026-10-25.

title: SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015
authors_year: SEBI consolidated landing page, amended 15 October 2026
learned: Official consolidated reporting/disclosure reference; the page identifies the amendment date.
implemented: Preserve reporting dates and separate publication/receipt times on manual financial and ownership observations.
not_implemented: Automated filings, compliance checks or current disclosure-deadline enforcement.
limitations: No reporting deadline or freshness threshold in the app is represented as a legally verified deadline.
verification: Official landing page and PDF link verified only; current operative deadlines not read. NSE shareholding/FII-DII pages timed out. Checked 2026-10-25.
